entry.title: Atlas Sound Surprise Releases First Album in 15 Years
entry.summary: Behold Thanatos
entry.content:
Atlas Sound is back: Thanatos, the first album in 15 years from the Bradford Cox project, is out now on streaming services. A vinyl release will follow next year, via 4AD. For now, you can listen along below with the visual aid of Cox’s “scent map,” and check out the accompanying video “A Visit With Bradford Cox.”

The surprise release follows a flurry of activity from the Deerhunter main brain, who returned to the stage at Making Time ∞ festival in September before releasing “Octoberland,” his first single since Parallax, last month. His two bands had mostly lain dormant since 2019, the year Deerhunter released Why Hasn’t Everything Already Disappeared?

Thanatos completes the trilogy of Logos and Parallax, a press release noted. Cox performed all the instruments and vocals before handing the record to Heba Kadry for mastering. His dog Faulkner is credited with emotional support in the studio. The album art, photographed by Javier Morales, depicts a sculpture by Chris Reynolds.

In an album bio, Cox’s longtime collaborator Cate Le Bon wrote, in part, “Virginia Woolf accessed her enormous eye by leaving the house. Bradford Cox finds it by burrowing deeper inside the familiar shell that is his home. Sheltered from all exterior weather fronts. surrounded by objects he has collected and absorbed for decades and held by the warmth of the love of his life. He has consumed it all and transformed geometrical space into a living burial chamber where he can shed the self.”

The album, she added, is “lyrically led by a disassociated primordial wisdom usually found in the sediment of dreams. A feeling you cannot name but it scratches at the heart and soul. Elusive but knowable. It is the past sung without memory of it but evoked by an action, a gesture, a ritual, a will. A means to access and revise an incomprehensible truth that you slept without knowing a loved one once.”

entry.title: Here’s Every Rapper Who Appears in GTA VI
entry.summary: You’ll run into Sexyy Red, Gucci Mane, Trina, JT, and many more in Vice City
entry.content:
On the off chance you’ve been dwelling beneath a rock at the bottom of the ocean, Grand Theft Auto VI arrived to rapturous praise today after a long 13-year wait. The game loosely follows protagonists Jason and Lucia as they wreak havoc (and have a few nice beach dates) around a version of Miami dubbed Vice City. But one of GTA VI’s most formidable achievements is its open world, which gathers a hefty cast of characters and thousands more NPCs.

It wouldn’t be a GTA game without heavy hip-hop influence. As far back as 2001’s GTA III (the first installment to include an all-rap in-game radio station, Game FM), the franchise has championed both mainstream hip-hop and bubbling regional scenes, inviting rappers to create original music for the series and voice characters of their own. GTA VI is no different, and comes equipped with an original soundtrack featuring Travis Scott, Young Thug, Gunna, Yung Lean, Playboi Carti, and more. It also premieres swath of new in-house stations, tapping hosts from the City Girl herself JT to Southern legends Trick Daddy and Trina.

Below, dive into a comprehensive list of all the rappers who make cameos—or portray full-fledged characters—in GTA VI. Happy carjacking.

Freddie Gibbs as Freddie

Denzel Curry as DWNPLY, a local rapper

Kodak Black as Himself

Sexyy Red as Herself

The Alchemist as Himself

Hood Brat as Bae-Luxe, one-half of the influencer rap duo Real Dimez

Krissy Celess as Roxy Rashad/Roxy, the other half of the influencer rap duo Real Dimez

N.O.R.E. as Himself

Gucci Mane as Himself

Trina as Herself

Trick Daddy as Himself

JT as DJ JT, co-host of Vice City Rap Radio

entry.title: A Guide to the GTA VI Radio Stations
entry.summary: Now’s your chance to hear Jeremy Irons DJ
entry.content:
As if getting Lana Del Rey’s husband wasn’t enough of a coup, Rockstar Games ended up recruiting an even wider range of notable artists and actors to host GTA VI’s in-house radio stations, which the company kept secret until the game premiered this week. Among the list are PinkPantheress, the Dare, Lindsey Buckingham, “Weird Al” Yankovic, JT, Brigitte Nielsen, Jeremy Irons (this is surely the first time that grouping has been mentioned in the same sentence). We’ve compiled a handy cheat sheet running down each station, their respective hosts, and the music they play below. Sadly, Tinashe was not invited to DJ so she had to uplift herself. Needless to say, this list is likely incomplete, so we’ll come back to update it as we make our way through the rest of the game.

The Nigerian superstar and Berlin DJ unite for a battery of generation-spanning, pan-African heaters. Afrobeats and amapiano rub shoulders with classic highlife, disco, and beyond.

Country classics are the order of the day, served up by Morgan Wallen (alter ego: MW) and, as Delta Dawn, Lana Del Rey. The latter’s partner, Jeremy Dufrene, cameos as “roving reporter, swamp meteorologist, and airboat captain” Mud Dog Mike.

Hosted by two Slayer honchos, Vice City’s resident metal station includes a premiere of Power Trip’s “Mutual Death Warrant.”

Rockstar’s joint enterprise with the Ibiza party CircoLoco extends into the game’s virtual world with this aural joyride around clubland.

Join a carnival of reggaeton, dembow, and bachata with chirpy hosts El Martillo and La Gata, better known as Bad Bunny and RaiNao. As RaiNao told Pitchfork, “Cocoteo gets our vibe, our slang, our taste, our pride, our experiences, our traditions, and all our crazy antics.”

JT is not the only Dade County luminary on the game’s airwaves: Dirty South Classics invites rappers Trick Daddy and Trina to stage a showcase of Southern all-timers including Outkast, Lil Wayne, and Gucci Mane.

The Power 105.1 staples present an alternate-reality morning show.

Host: Doug Stanhope An old GTA favorite returns for those who want to go hard with some soft-rock classics.

The modern counterpart to Vice City FM, Flash FM returns with marquee pop hits and new hosts. Robyn herself has a pair of tunes in the mix: vintage selection “Show Me Love” and the Sexistentially revamped classic “Blow My Mind.”

A murderers’ row of blues legends, from Sister Rosetta Tharpe to Ella Fitzgerald, populates this station, hosted by blues legend Buddy Guy and blues progeny Keith Richards

The two TLC members activate cruise control for a sun-dappled parade of silky-smooth, feelgood ’90s R&B.

This spoof and spin-of station from Honey FM features Craig Robinson spinning original songs including “Finger Bang My Heart” by BJ The Chicago Kid

Initially kept under wraps, this curiosity-piquing station showcases global singers who interpret pop classics. It is staffed by the august British actor Jeremy Irons, in character as one DJ Dicky.

Jazz fusion heads will be nodding to the Brecker Brothers and beyond on the connoisseurs’ choice of Leonida stations.

Like the abuelita rocking on the porch outside Cocoteo FM headquarters, Radio La Ola spins golden-age Latin classics from the likes of host Gloria Estefan and Willie Colón.

Inspired by Adrian Sherwood’s record label, Radio On-U inhales the vibe-heavy, vintage sounds of Jamaica, from roots reggae to lovers rock.

Get your fill of electroclash, indietronica, synth-rock sleaze, and leftfield pop from the likes of LCD Soundsystem and Fischerspooner, with your cheeky hosts Victoria (PinkPantheress) and Harrison (the Dare).

Dig out your bowtie and hold onto your hat for this helter-skelter of high-stakes classical music, from Profokiev to Mahler, hosted by pianist Yuja Wang

The onetime home of GTA’s heavy-metal contingent has sold out and gone classic rock for GTA VI: Buckle up for Bon Jovi, Kiss, REO Speedwagon, and Van Halen.

The home station of GTA’s storied metropolis is a non-stop 1980s pop party hosted by none other than “Weird Al” Yankovic, who also wrote in-game commercials and voiced the Burger Shot ads. “As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn’t be more excited about this,” he wrote on Instagram. “Now if you’ll excuse me, I’ve got to get back to playing the game!”

Surefire rap hits from A-listers such as Drake, Cardi B, and Playboi Carti cascade through Vice City in this station from the endlessly charismatic City Girls rapper JT.

The Florida rapper appears in a secret radio station—one you can reportedly only get by unlocking an in-game puzzle—that features Haitian and Haitian-American artists.

Another talk show, this one filled with trivia from the Leonida area.

Satirical conservative talk radio station WKTT reportedly introduces Cum Town native Stavros Halkias to Liberty City. The comedian’s apparent parody has drawn the unperturbed attention of far-right blusterers Alex Jones and Nick Fuentes.

Named for Gilles Peterson’s eclectic real-life station, GTA’s Worldwide FM conjures a cosmos of otherworldly funk, soul, and jazz. An extremely unconfirmed rumor points to There in fact is an unreleased D’Angelo song in the mix, apparently titled “Kamikaze,” per the official credits.

Unlockable within the game’s Vault Nightclub, this is the stuffy techno dancefloor hidden away in the game’s grimy underworld.

entry.title: Beabadoobee Goes Bananas 4 Cats on New Album and Song
entry.summary: “No Punctuation” leads the indie rock singer-songwriter’s quick follow-up to Pylon
entry.content:
Beabadoobee released her fourth album in September, and now she’s already prepped to drop her next LP in mere months. Bananas 4 Cats, the follow-up to Pylon, arrives February 19 via Dirty Hit/Interscope. Give the lead single, “No Punctuation,” a listen below while fawning over Beabadoobee’s real-life pet cats Kimchi and Miso (who even have their own merch).

“No Punctuation” was a long time coming for fans, as Beabadoobee shared snippets of the song over the past four years, only to add it into her setlist earlier this week. The rest of the material on Bananas 4 Cats, however, is more recent. “I just needed to write an album like this after Pylon,” Beabadoobee said in a press release. “It happened naturally, I got back home and felt inspired, and made another album.”

In fact, Pylon is so recent that Beabadoobee is still in the midst of her initial tour for the album. She’s still got dozens of dates left on that tour schedule, including a performance at Primavera Sound Porto next year. Pylon features a number of alt-rock guest stars—including members of Turnstile, Deftones, Paramore, and Pinegrove—and became Beabadoobee’s second album to hit No. 1 on the UK charts, following 2024’s This Is How Tomorrow Moves.

Revisit Quinn Moreland’s interview Shopping in Brooklyn With Beabadoobee, Grunge-Pop Sweetheart.

entry.title: Phoebe Bridgers Covers Adrianne Lenker’s “Anything” for the Holidays
entry.summary: Proceeds from the track will benefit Palestine Children’s Relief Fund
entry.content:
Phoebe Bridgers’ holiday songbook continues to grow. Today, she’s releasing a cover of Adrianne Lenker’s 2020 single “Anything,” which ropes together Christmas Eve anecdotes, tears spilled in the car, and unbreakable longing. This rendition was co-produced by Bridgers, Jack Antonoff, Tony Berg, and Ethan Gruska. Both Bridgers’ and Lenker’s proceeds from the benefit single will go to Palestine Children’s Relief Fund. Give it a listen below.

By now, Bridgers has made a habit of recording Christmas cover songs to raise money for charities. She previously put her own spin on the classic “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” Tom Waits’ “Day After Tomorrow,” Simon & Garfunkel’s “7 O’Clock News / Silent Night” with Fiona Apple and the National’s Matt Berninger, Merle Haggard’s “If We Make It Through December,” McCarthy Trenching’s “Christmas Song” with Jackson Browne, and the Handsome Family’s “So Much Wine.” Her supergroup Boygenius also joined in the tradition with a 2023 cover of “The Parting Glass” with Ye Vagabonds.

Bridgers is still riding high on her seven Grammy nominations tied to Lost Weekend, which is in the running for Best Alternative Album, and her recent stop on Saturday Night Live, where she performed “Bobby” and “Still Standing.” If you missed the chance to see her headlining tour in support of the LP, there’s still time: she added a bunch of new tour dates in North America in 2027.

“Anything” originally appeared on Lenker’s 2020 solo album Songs / Instrumentals. Lenker followed that record with the solo LP Bright Future in 2024 and Live at Revolution Hall the following year. These days, she’s gearing up for Big Thief’s return to the stage with a 2027 tour.

Read about Bridgers’ Punisher and Lenker’s Songs / Instrumentals in The 50 Best Albums of 2020.

entry.title: Watch Taylor Swift Bring “Our Song” Medley to 2026 CMA Awards
entry.summary: Her first time playing the ceremony in 13 years
entry.content:
Taylor Swift made her return to the CMA Awards stage in Nashville tonight, performing for the first time since 2013. Clad in bejeweled cowboy boots (customary attire for such an occasion), she delivered a medley of her Toy Story 5 track “I Knew It, I Knew You” and her 2006 hit “Our Song.” Watch it below.

“I Knew It, I Knew You” was up for Single of the Year at the CMA Awards, ultimately losing out to Ella Langley’s juggernaut “Choosin’ Texas.” Award or not, it signaled a successful return to the country music space for Swift, becoming her first track to debut in the top 10 of Billboard’s Country Airplay Chart, since “Red." She’ll have another chance to win some hardware for the song at the 2027 Grammy Awards, where it’s nominated for Best Song Written for Visual Media. She’ll also face off against Langley in three of the big four categories. The Life of a Showgirl is up against Langley’s Dandelion, “The Fate of Ophelia” and “Choosin’ Texas” are both nominated for Song and Record of the Year.

In September, Swift augmented the original TLOS with four new songs, packaging the new release as The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore. One of those tracks,“Patient Zero,” came complete with a Swift-directed music video starring Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell, which Swift premiered at the MTV Video Music Awards, where she received the inaugural Artist Director Honors.

entry.title: Waxahatchee Is Hosting a Songwriting Workshop
entry.summary: Katie Crutchfield will host four weeks of online classes via School of Song
entry.content:
Waxahatchee’s Katie Crutchfield is doing her part to rid the world of bad music by sharing her songwriting secrets in a Zoom workshop early next year. Following in the pedagogic footsteps of Phil Elverum and Adrianne Lenker, the singer-songwriter will present four classes and lead three Q&As for the School of Song platform this coming January. You can enroll here for the price of $200.

The class offers a subsidiary benefit to Crutchfield, who is currently working on a Tigers Blood follow-up, she wrote on Substack. “I have a long term fear of public speaking. It’s why I don’t really speak on stage at my shows. This workshop will help me face that fear head on a bit which I’m legitimately excited about. Even more notable is that I am in the early phases of writing my next record. I think it’s the perfect moment to unpack my songwriting process (a seasoned, old process at this point, occasionally in need of a dusting off) and poke around a bit. I’m excited to share things, excited to learn things, excited to see if I knock something loose for myself in the process.”

The course description posits a number of interesting topics, such as how Crutchfield discovers “lyrics within the structure of her melodies” and how “a melodic idea can suggest the sounds and rhythms that the lyrics can follow, and how listening to those cues can unlock a stubborn line.” She also proposes a songwriting paradigm that aspires to the “Perfectly Descriptive” or the “Perfectly Poetic,” either choosing to describe “a lived experience or emotional state” or foregoing “perfect sense” in favor of “something purely poetical.”

How Waxahatchee Made the Album of Her (Second) Life

entry.title: SML Announce 2027 U.S. Tour
entry.summary: Including an opening slot for Death Cab for Cutie at Red Rocks
entry.content:
Los Angeles-based jazz quintet SML are ready to bring their live experience on the road again in 2027. They’ve announced a short run of U.S. tour dates set for next spring, beginning in San Francisco on March 11. Among the highlights is an unexpected pairing and place: an opening gig for Death Cab for Cutie at Colorado’s famed Red Rocks Amphitheatre. Check out SML’s complete list of tour dates below.

The five artists behind SML—Anna Butterss, Jeremiah Chiu, Josh Johnson, Booker Stardrum, and Gregory Uhlmann—are busy with their own solo careers, but especially together in SML as of late. As previously announced, they’re slated to perform at Big Ears Festival next year, and earlier this summer they released the live album Spontaneous Music Live. Meanwhile, Johnson just dropped his own solo album, Animative, a few weeks ago.

entry.title: Harold Budd and Robin Guthrie’s Mysterious Skin Score Coming to Vinyl
entry.summary: “Much more than mere background music: It’s the heart and soul of the whole movie,” says director Gregg Araki
entry.content:
Long out of print and confined to a digital wilderness, Harold Budd and Robin Guthrie’s score to the cult favorite Gregg Araki movie Mysterious Skin is getting a new reissue from 4AD. Set for its first-ever vinyl release, as well as a CD reissue, Music From the Film Mysterious Skin is due out January 29. Cocteau Twin Guthrie remastered the collaboration in tandem with a recent 4K restoration of the film for its 20th anniversary.

Araki said in a press release:

I’ve been a huge fan of Robin and Harold’s since the 80’s glory days when 4AD, Cocteau Twins, and The White Arcades ruled and shaped my world. This music has been such an essential part of my life and such a profound influence on me and my work. I always listen to music when I write - as does Scott Heim, author of the original novel Mysterious Skin—so this soundtrack is much, much more than mere background music: it’s the heart and soul of the whole movie. The dreamy poetic nature of both the book and the film comes directly from this style of music—and the incredible score Robin and Harold have composed is so evocative and breathtakingly gorgeous, it literally brought me to tears the first time I heard it.

Music From the Film Mysterious Skin was the first in a string of duo albums from Guthrie and Budd, nearly two decades after they first worked together on The Moon and the Melodies. They continued to collaborate until Budd’s death in 2020.

Harold Budd and Robin Guthrie: Music from the Film Mysterious Skin
$31.99 at Rough Trade

entry.title: Listen to Erika de Casier’s New Song “Whispers”
entry.summary: The track was co-produced by Bladee and Yung Lean collaborator Eurohead
entry.content:
Danish crooner Erika de Casier is back with a new standalone single: “Whispers.” The song was co-produced by Bladee and Yung Lean collaborator Eurohead, and comes with a music video directed by Igor Pjörrt, in which she and Atusa Zamani run across the scalloped beaches of an oceanside property before waking up at night inside a car. Watch it below.

“Whispers” is De Casier’s first song since surprise-releasing Lifetime in May of last year. She teased that record with a handful of white-label cassettes on Bandcamp that sold out immediately, before officially dropping the album online for everyone to hear. That fall, she went on a brief tour in support of the LP, in addition to opening for Lorde and Robyn on select dates.

Read about Lifetime in The 50 Best Albums of 2025.

entry.title: Belle and Sebastian Reissuing If You’re Feeling Sinister With New Rarities Album
entry.summary: Listen to the unearthed “Colette and the Mystery Girl” from bonus LP Lisa Helps the Blind
entry.content:
Belle and Sebastian are celebrating the 30th anniversary of If You’re Feeling Sinister with a new, bumper reissue that includes a full album of rarities. The band has paired its classic 1996 album (well, one of them) with Lisa Helps the Blind, a 13-track trove of unreleased songs, demos, and field recordings made between 1995 and 1997. Listen to one of the unvaulted songs, “Colette and the Mystery Girl,” below; Murdoch recorded the track with friends in a kitchen in 1994, a press release notes. Matador is putting out the reissue, licensed from Bella Figura, on January 20.

A 2xLP edition, shipping next March, features new essays from Stuart Murdoch and the author Damien Love. An excerpt from Murdoch’s explains that the title Lisa Helps the Blind came from “a headline in the Glasgow Evening Times about a girl who was working with blind people.” He adds, “We knew of Lisa because she danced up at the Art School on a Saturday. We never talked to her though, she ran with another crowd, but she was undeniably glam and beautiful. We built her up in our imaginations—helping the blind by day, dancing and being fabulous by night.”

Read more about If You’re Feeling Sinister’s “Kinksian charm and anti-social chestnuts” in The 100 Best Indie Rock Albums of All Time.

entry.title: Don Toliver Releasing New Album Nitrous Next Month
entry.summary: The Cactus Jack artist is following his Grammy nominations splash with a self-produced, second LP of the year
entry.content:
Don Toliver has set a December 4 release date for Nitrous, his second album of 2026. The Texan rapper-producer is coming off the back of a major 2026 run that crested this week with five Grammy nominations—including for Best New Artist—behind his chart-topping January album Octane. The new LP, which is self-produced and -engineered, arrives the day before Toliver’s SNL debut.

The single “Party With the Boys,” released last Friday with a video starring Bam Margera, will feature on the album, according to a press release. Cactus Jack will co-release Nitrous with Atlantic and his own Donnway & Co. Last month, Toliver united with Drake to remix another Best New Artist contender, Ella Langley.

entry.title: Billie Eilish, Harry Styles, and Sam Fender Headlining Glastonbury 2027
entry.summary: Cher returns to the stage in the “legend slot,” with Massive Attack, the xx, and Kraftwerk also on the lineup
entry.content:
Glastonbury has announced its youngest headliners in years. Billie Eilish, Harry Styles, and Sam Fender will take the top slots at the storied UK festival’s 2027 edition, with Cher as the unofficial fourth headliner in the Sunday-afternoon “legends slot.” Given second billing on the poster are Massive Attack, Kraftwerk, Lily Allen, Little Simz, Ezra Collective, and the xx. Find the first-wave poster below.

Joining Kraftwerk, Cher, and Styles in making their Glastonbury debuts are Angine de Poitrine, the Womack Sisters, and Sombr. (Eilish headlined in 2022, with Fender playing second fiddle.) Other initial performers include emissaries of pop (FKA twigs, Robyn, Underscores), rock (the War on Drugs, Dinosaur Jr., King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard), dance (Basement Jaxx, the Avalanches, Bonobo), R&B (Thundercat, Leon Bridges, Nao), and British royalty (the Streets, Blood Orange, Hot Chip).

Last year, the festival took one of its regular fallow years to allow the grounds to recover. The 2025 headliners were the 1975, Neil Young, and Olivia Rodrigo.

entry.title: Director of MGMT’s “Kids” and “Time to Pretend” Videos Dies at 43
entry.summary: Filmmaker Ray Tintori also shot videos for Solange, Arcade Fire, and the Killers
entry.content:
Ray Tintori, the filmmaker behind MGMT’s breakout Oracular Spectacular videos, has died, People and TMZ report. He was 43. No cause was provided, and his death is under investigation, according to both publications, citing the New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner.

Born into a filmmaking family, Tintori started making shorts—Jettison Your Loved Ones and his award-winning thesis film Death to the Tinman—in the mid 2000s, before his break with the music videos for MGMT’s “Time to Pretend,” “Electric Feel,” and “Kids.” His fantastical sets and special effects dovetailed with a cozy, handmade feel that characterized his ongoing work. The “Kids” video starred Joanna Newsom as a mother oblivious to the writhing monsters that pursued her terrified toddler. (A behind-the-scenes short put to bed some lingering questions over whether the experience was a little harsh on the real-life toddler.) Tintori returned to work with MGMT on his final video, for the band’s Christine and the Queens collaboration “Dancing in Babylon.”

In the meantime, Tintori notched up a résumé that included the Killers’ “Spaceman,” Arcade Fire’s “Chemistry,” and Chairlift’s perpetually melting “Evident Utensil” visual. He contributed to the acclaimed magical realist drama Beasts of the Southern Wild, a product of the Court 13 collective he co-founded. Last year, Tintori co-directed a New York stage production of Ethan Coen’s Waiting and cameoed as a newsreel photographer in Marty Supreme.

entry.title: Superchunk Set 2027 North American Tour
entry.summary: New Merge signee Tanner York will support the band on the spring run
entry.content:
Superchunk have announced a 2027 North American tour, set to launch next spring. The trek, which New York-based power pop artist Tanner York is opening for, begins in Norfolk, Virginia on March 12 and concludes with a homecoming show in Carrboro, North Carolina on March 27. That final date will also include Lambchop.

After they conclude the North American run, Superchunk will head to Japan to play five shows across Hiroshima, Osaka, Nagoya, and Tokyo. The band shared their most recent album, Songs in the Key of Yikes, in 2025.

Read about Superchunk’s Here’s Where the Strings Come In at No. 44 in The 100 Best Indie Rock Albums of All Time.

entry.title: Big Thief Plots 2027 U.S. Tour
entry.summary: The trio will hit Portland, New York, Pittsburgh, and more next summer
entry.content:
If you missed Big Thief’s Ryman Auditorium show earlier this year, where they debuted all 29 songs from their forthcoming triple album Horsepower, you’re in luck: the trio will embark on a short U.S. tour in 2027. To allow ample time for the group to get through all the new (and old) material, they will perform sans opener, and instead include two sets with an intermission. The trek will kick off in June in Portland, Maine, and stop in New York, Pittsburgh, Richmond, and more before a final show in Columbus. Scroll down for the full schedule.

Read Jeremy Larson’s feature, Our First Impressions of Horsepower, Big Thief’s Upcoming Triple Album.
